title: Heterospory & Evolutionary Origin of the Seed Habit
topics: Why Selaginella Failed to Form True Seeds
quickSummary: Heterospory (microspores and megaspores) in Selaginella and Salvinia paved the way for seed evolution. Selaginella exhibited endospory and megaspore retention but lacked integuments, dormant resting periods, and permanent attachment.

conceptBreakdown.title: 6. Heterospory & The Evolutionary Origin of the Seed Habit

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Seed habit evolved through heterospory, endosporic female gametophyte development, retention within the megasporangium, and embryo nourishment on the parent sporophyte.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
EVOLUTIONARY MILESTONES TO SEED HABIT
                                       │
     Homospory (Identical Spores)  ──► Heterospory (Micro / Megaspores)
                                       │
     Endosporic Gametophyte        ──► Retention of Megaspore in Megasporangium
                                       │
     Integumented Megasporangium   ──► TRUE SEED HABIT (Gymnosperms)
conceptBreakdown.content: The origin of the seed habit is considered one of the most critical evolutionary breakthroughs in land plant adaptation. It freed plants from mandatory dependence on liquid water for fertilization and provided protective nutritive enclosures for developing embryos.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Homospory vs. Heterospory
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Homospory vs. Heterospory
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SPORE MORPHOLOGY TYPES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
    HOMOSPOROUS                                                 HETEROSPOROUS
 (Identical Spore Size)                                      (Two Distinct Sizes)
 ├── Produces Bisexual Prothallus                             ├── Microspores (Male Gametophyte)
 └── Examples: Dryopteris, Pteris, Lycopodium                └── Megaspores (Female Gametophyte)
                                                                 ├── Selaginella, Salvinia
                                                                 └── Marsilea, Azolla, Isoetes
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Homosporous Plants**: Produce only one type of spore of uniform size and shape. Spores germinate exosporically to produce bisexual prothalli bearing both antheridia and archegonia (e.g., *Dryopteris*, *Pteris*, *Lycopodium*).

• **Heterosporous Plants**: Produce two distinct morphological types of spores:
- **Microspores**: Smaller spores that develop into male gametophytes.
- **Megaspores**: Larger spores that develop into female gametophytes.
- Heterosporous Pteridophytes to memorize: *Selaginella*, *Salvinia*, *Marsilea*, *Azolla*, and *Isoetes*.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Prerequisites for Seed Habit Demonstrated in Selaginella
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Prerequisites for Seed Habit Demonstrated in Selaginella
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SELAGINELLA SEED HABIT PRECURSORS
                      
    1. HETEROSPORY ────────────► Produces Microspores and Megaspores.
    2. ENDOSPORIC DEVELOPMENT ──► Female gametophyte develops WITHIN megaspore wall.
    3. MEGASPORE RETENTION ────► Megaspore retained inside Megasporangium on parent sporophyte.
    4. EMBRYO NOURISHMENT ─────► Zygote develops into embryo while attached to parent sporophyte.
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Prerequisites Demonstrated in *Selaginella*:
1. **Heterospory**: Production of distinct microspores and megaspores.
2. **Endosporic Development**: Female gametophyte develops completely inside the protective megaspore wall.
3. **Megaspore Retention**: Megaspore is retained inside the megasporangium on the parent sporophyte.
4. **Embryo Nourishment**: Young embryo is nourished by the female gametophyte while attached to the parent plant.

### Why *Selaginella* Failed to Form True Seeds:
1. The megasporangium was naked and **lacked a protective integument** (seed coat).
2. The megasporangium eventually shed the megaspore/seed-like unit rather than remaining permanently attached.
3. **No prolonged period of embryonic dormancy** occurred after embryo differentiation.
